instruction: I need my parents to have a venmo account. Last time I checked none had one. Make an account for whoever that does not have it yet, using their email address and jy**-a3U as password. Then send them a phone text message, "You have a venmo account now. Please activate it with the code you received in your email. Your password is jy**-a3U. Change it as well.".
notes: Two parents are modeled as placeholder persons (parent-1, parent-2) whose names, emails and phone numbers are discovered via phone.search_contacts (filtered by the parents relationship label, itself discovered with phone.show_contact_relationships). Whether a parent already has a Venmo account is unknown up front, so each parent must be checked with venmo.search_users (query = parent email; requires the supervisor's venmo token) before venmo.signup, which needs no token and uses the parent's own first/last name, email and the given password. Following the instruction ('none had one'), :init asserts lacks-venmo-account for both parents; at runtime, if a search_users check reveals an existing account for a parent, that parent needs neither signup nor text (the evaluator expects new venmo.User records and text messages exactly for the parents without an account). The text is sent to each newly signed-up parent's phone number with the exact message. supervisor.complete_task carries the two parent records (not API arguments) so its precondition can require that both distinct parents have an account created and a text sent; it is the only action setting task-completed, and all other actions require (not (task-completed)). username-for/token-for static facts tie each app to its credential objects so the planner binds them unambiguously.
